title: Lotus on dark water
request: Make a shader: a lotus opening on dark water

steps.plan: Night pond scene, done in 2D with a perspective water plane. Sky: a dark blue gradient above a horizon line, with hashed twinkling stars, a small moon and its glow. Water: everything below the horizon is mapped to plane coordinates (depth = 1/(horizon - y), lateral = x*depth), so ripples and lily pads foreshorten correctly. Concentric ripple rings spread from the stem plus a slow swell. The ripple height offsets the lookup used for the mirrored flower reflection, and also breaks up a moon glitter streak. Fresnel brightens the water toward the horizon. Lily pads: notched discs in plane coordinates with radial veins, a rim and gentle bobbing, antialiased with fwidth. Lotus: three layers of petals plus a seed pod, composited back to front with premultiplied alpha. Each petal is an almond-shaped vesica SDF, narrowed at the base, with a slight cupping bend. Each petal casts a soft shadow on the layers behind it. Petal colour runs from a cream base to pink tips, with veins and a darker rim. Layer brightness rises from back to front. The back layer has 5 petals, the middle 4 and the front 3; the front centre petal shortens as if tilting toward the viewer. The open amount o loops slowly through 0.5-0.5cos(t), smoothed. It fans the petal angles from a closed bud to nearly horizontal and reveals the yellow stamen ring and seed pod. The stem sways a little. Extras: a soft pink halo, drifting fireflies, a vignette and gamma.

steps.critique: The scene reads well as dark water at night: moon, glittering moon path, stars, lily pads, drifting firefly glows, and a pink lotus on a stem with a reflection. The central idea, the lotus opening, barely happens. Across 0–3s the bud stays a closed teardrop. Only at 3s do the tips start to separate into a few small points. A viewer sampling these frames would see a static bud rather than a blooming flower. The bud is also a single flat shape with vertical stripes, not distinct overlapping petals, so even a full opening may not look like petals unfolding. The reflection is cropped at the bottom edge. The stem looks detached: it sits above the waterline with no ripple where it meets the water.
fixes: Speed up the bloom so it is clearly visible within a few seconds, e.g. open = smoothstep(0.0, 4.0, mod(iTime, 10.0)), or a slow ping-pong with 0.5 - 0.5*cos(iTime*0.6).

Build the flower from 6–10 separate petal SDFs, each an ellipse rotated about the base point. Rotate each petal outward by angle_i * open, with an inner and outer ring, so the opening is a real spreading of petals and not just notching the bud tips.
Shade each petal individually: darker pink at the edges, a white-yellow base gradient, and draw back petals behind front ones by layering.
When open is above about 0.6, reveal a yellow seed-pod/stamen disc in the centre.
Move the flower up, or the horizon, so the full reflection fits on screen. Distort the reflection with the same ripple noise used for the moon path.
Add a small expanding ring ripple where the stem meets the water: a sin(length(p - base)*40 - iTime*3) band faded with distance.

steps.plan: This revision makes the bloom happen on screen, makes the petals read as separate shapes, fits the reflection on screen and seats the stem in the water. Bloom: the open amount is now o = 0.5-0.5cos(0.8t+0.6), a ping-pong of about 8 s. It is near-closed at t=0, half open at 1.5 s and fully open at 3 s. Petals: 12 separate almond (vesica) SDF petals plus 2 green sepals, all rotated about a shared base point. They sit in three layers drawn back to front (5 back, 4 middle, 3 front). Each layer fans outward by angle_i*spread(o), and even the closed bud keeps a small fan so the tips read as separate petals. The outer petals bend outward as they open. Each petal is shaded on its own: a white-yellow base, a pink tip gradient, a centre crease, darkened sides, a deep pink rim and fine veins. A slight per-petal hue shift plus a drop shadow onto the layer behind keeps them distinct. The yellow stamen ring and the green seed pod with seed holes are revealed once o passes about 0.4. Layout: the horizon is raised to 0.3, the waterline to -0.08 and the flower is a bit smaller. The mirrored reflection now fits inside the frame. The reflection lookup is offset by the same ripple height field that breaks up the moon glitter path. Stem contact: an expanding ring ripple, computed in perspective water-plane coordinates around the stem base, adds bright crests and a soft dark contact ring. A lily pad is moved out of the reflection's way. Kept from before: the sky, stars, moon, glitter path, pads, halo, fireflies and vignette.

steps.critique: The frames clearly show a lotus opening on dark water. At 0s it is a closed bud, at 1.5s it is half open, and at 3s it is fully open with layered pink petals. The night water reads well, with lily pads, concentric ripples, a moon with its glittering reflection path, stars and fireflies, so the main idea and the motion are both there. Problems: 1) The reflection is a near-literal mirror of the flower placed directly below the stem. It sits on top of the ripple rings with no ripple distortion and looks like a second flower rather than a reflection, and it is about as bright as the flower itself. 2) The flower floats above the stem attachment point, and the stem is a thin line ending at the ripple centre, so the bloom reads as hovering. 3) The 'dark water' is fairly bright and hazy grey-purple (average brightness 0.24), with low contrast. 4) The petals are pink at the tips and white in the middle, with no visible centre or seed pod once open.
fixes: Distort the reflection: offset its sample uv.x by sin(uv.y*40.0 + iTime*2.0)*0.01*depth, scale its brightness to about 0.4, and fade it with distance below the waterline.
Darken the water base colour (e.g. vec3(0.03,0.04,0.07)) and add a vignette so the flower and moon path stand out more.
Anchor the flower on the water: bring the bloom's base down to the waterline, and drop the visible stem or replace it with a short dark pad under the flower.
Once openness > 0.7, add a yellow-green seed pod / stamen disc at the flower's centre.
Add a subtle per-petal sway (rotate each petal by sin(iTime + i)*0.03) so the flower keeps moving after it is fully open.
